purpose: Tipranavir is used to treat HIV infection in adults and children who have already tried other HIV medicines that are no longer working well. It is always used together with other HIV medications, never alone. It helps lower the amount of HIV virus in your body and keeps your immune system stronger.
how_it_works: HIV uses a special tool called a protease enzyme to make copies of itself inside your body. Tipranavir blocks that enzyme, like putting a wrench in the gears, so the virus cannot make working copies of itself. This helps slow down the spread of HIV in your body.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, tiredness, and headache are the most common side effects. Some people also notice increased fat in certain areas of the body or changes in cholesterol and blood sugar levels.
warnings: Tipranavir can rarely cause serious liver problems, including liver failure — tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual stomach pain. It can also rarely cause bleeding in the brain, especially if you take blood thinners. This medicine contains alcohol and should not be used with certain other drugs. If you are pregnant, talk to your doctor before taking it. Always take it with ritonavir as prescribed.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 500 mg (two 250 mg capsules) taken twice a day, always together with 200 mg of ritonavir. It should be taken with food to help it work better and reduce stomach upset. For children, the dose is based on body weight and is calculated by your doctor.
